transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Ukraine's resumed its attacks on Russia's oil refineries over President Trump's objections.
President Volodymyr Zelensky tells the Financial Times he held off briefly, but note not anymore.
That is one sign of division between Zelensky and Trump.
NPR's Greg Myry reports that another involves a disruption to the satellite communication system on which Ukraine's war effort relies.
Ukraine's defense ministry is saying that this satellite network is back and working as normal.
And by way of explanation, many people know the satellite communication system Starlink.
This is part of Elon Musk's empire.
But there's also a military version called Star Shield that he built for the U.S. government and military.
The Pentagon shares this with Ukraine, which uses it to guide its drones.
But yesterday, Ukraine discovered quite abruptly that the Star Shield system had suddenly been greatly restricted.
NPR's Greg Myry.
Earlier this month, President Trump blamed Ukraine's attacks on Russia's oil refineries for the record high diesel prices in the U.S.
that have proven to be a midterm election year liability for Republicans.
The president is back from a days long midterm campaign blitz to Republican strongholds and Piers Tamara Keith has more.
In September, Trump was speaking to a group of Republicans in competitive races when he pledged to spend the final 30 days before the midterms campaigning for them.
Since then, he's only campaigned with a handful of them.
Republican Party chairman Joe Gruders.
Everything changes every week, but the most important thing we're focused on is turnout and driving the base out and there's no better person in the country than President Donald J. Trump.
He's an absolute machine.
Trump's travels have taken him to a lot of traditionally Republican states.
A reflection of where he can help, but also of a shifting landscape where even red state Republicans need a boost.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
One dominant voter issue, data centers. Oregon has paused permitting for new ones.
It joins two other states with similar data center moratoriums. Oregon Public Broadcasting's April Ehrlich has details.
Oregon's Democratic Governor Tina Kotek directed the state's environmental regulators to stop permitting new or expanding data centers until July.
The directive comes amid an unusually tight race for governor between Kotek and a Republican candidate, state Senator Christine Drazen.
Oregon hasn't elected a Republican governor since the 1980s.
Each candidate has accused each other of not doing enough to regulate Oregon's growing data center market.
Amazon is a big player here.
Its executives quickly criticized Kotek's directive as abrupt, saying it will help billions of dollars in planned investment.
New York and Texas have similar permitting moratoriums.
For NPR News, I'm April Ehrlich in Portland, Oregon.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
U.S. inflation may be higher, but customers are still willing to spend their money.
New government figures show retail sales rose 0.8 percent last month.
The International Monetary Fund's just provided a video update of its regional economic outlook for sub-Saharan Africa.
It finds economies appear to be managing the energy crisis resulting from the U.S. and Israeli war with Iran.
Zayn Zaidan, head of the IMF's Africa Department, says growth is resilient, but prospects are uneven.
We project the region to grow by 4.5 percent in both 2026 and 2027.
The continent is facing higher inflation, high interest burdens, and a decline in aid.
A critically endangered frog in Ghana has been successfully bred in captivity.
Conservationists hope the feat could help save the super tiny and extraordinary species.
Here's NPR's Ari Daniel.
An adult Afia burago's puddle frog can easily fit on your thumbnail.
A mining project is threatening the frog's habitat, which could wipe them out.
So a group called Herp Conservation Ghana and the London Zoo teamed up to collect some frogs to rear in captivity.
Zookeeper Unar Iverson says the frogs have reproduced and there are now at least 15 froglets.
But it's very hard when you have next to no knowledge on that species.
I'm just over the moon and we're really optimistic about what their future kind of holds.
If the mine goes through, the team could take what they've learned in London to Ghana
to perhaps relocate the frogs to a compatible habitat nearby,
which they hope might protect the species from extinction.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries despite Trump's objections, Zelensky tells Financial Times
Ukraine says Pentagon-supplied Starlink military satellite system, Star Shield, is restored after abrupt restriction
Trump returns from midterm campaign blitz to Republican strongholds, campaigning less than he pledged
Oregon Governor Tina Kotek pauses permitting for new data centers until July amid governor race
U.S. retail sales rise 0.8 percent last month despite higher inflation
IMF projects sub-Saharan Africa growth of 4.5 percent in 2026 and 2027 despite inflation pressures
Critically endangered Ghanaian Afia Burago's puddle frog successfully bred in captivity at London Zoo
